title: Infrastructure Stability Intervention Decision Framework
description: State-to-action mapping for infrastructure stabilization. Multi-lever, phase-sequenced. Single-lever approaches fail because B_i, epsilon, L_f_active, and kappa interact nonlinearly.
core_principle: This is stability management under stress, not optimization to a fixed point. Goal is desynchronization of failure events and maximal system resilience given latent-node constraints. Levers are coupled. Order of operations is a constraint, not a preference.

marginal_high_sensitivity.note: Most dangerous regime. Does not appear as crisis in financial metrics. dPhi/dt is the critical signal.
marginal_high_sensitivity.time_sensitivity: interventions must begin within 6 months or correction cost multiplies

structural_decay.note: Single-lever approaches will fail. Coupled multi-lever deployment required.

L1.authority_note: A crew, union local, or community can traverse peer networks and validate competency without asking anyone. No statute grants or withholds the right to talk to people you already know.
L1.reversibility_note: A burned node does not un-burn. See ledger F-003 — the damage is to network topology, and topology does not recover on the timescale of a campaign.
L1.name: latent_node_activation
L1.description: Identify and activate suppressed high-skill nodes via lateral network traversal and competency-first validation.
L1.prerequisite_note: B_i reduction must precede or co-occur. Activating into high-B_i environment creates re-suppression and permanently reduces p_engage.
L1.effect_on_model: increases L_f_active via L_latent*p_engage channel — fast time constant relative to training pipeline

L2.authority_note: Requires whoever assigns work. A shift supervisor or crew lead can do it inside their own scope; no external permission needed.
L2.reversibility_note: A deployment assignment can be reversed next week at no structural cost.
L2.name: older_node_priority_deployment
L2.description: Front-load older high-R_i, high-L_f nodes into safety-critical roles and high-kappa interfaces. Use as hazard amplifiers and mentor hubs.
L2.effect_on_model: immediate L_f_active increase + R_i propagation to adjacent nodes + local kappa_effective reduction at deployment sites
L2.temporal_note: Creates temporal handoff window: older node contribution front-loads stability while younger nodes ramp. Monitor L_f_old(t) + L_f_young(t) for gap.

L3.authority_note: Credential gates are usually statutory or set by an accrediting body. A firm can build a parallel competency pathway inside its own hiring, but cannot remove the external gate.
L3.name: epsilon_reduction
L3.description: Reduce labor exclusion coefficient by replacing credential gates with competency validation pathways.
L3.effect_on_model: directly reduces epsilon in dL_f/dt equation, increasing L_f_active slope
L3.bifurcation_note: Bifurcation diagram shows epsilon is primary control parameter for long-run Phi. Minimum viable fidelity threshold visible in time-to-threshold sweep.

L4.authority_note: An alternative visibility channel is a bulletin board, a shared log, or a standing agenda item. Local hierarchy can be routed around without its consent, which is the entire point.
L4.name: B_i_reduction
L4.description: Reduce signal obstruction factor. Create alternative visibility channels for latent node contributions bypassing local hierarchy suppression.
L4.phase_constraint: MUST PRECEDE L1. This is not a preference. See re-suppression failure mode.
L4.effect_on_model: increases O_i*(1-B_i) in effective contribution formula, raises p_engage_i by demonstrating structural difference before commitment

L5.authority_note: Capital allocation. Requires whoever approves the expansion budget — a board, a council, a utility commission.
L5.reversibility_note: Throttled expansion can be un-throttled. This is the cheapest lever to undo and the easiest to restart, which is why it is the natural first ask of a reluctant board.
L5.name: complexity_growth_throttle
L5.description: Temporarily reduce rate of expansion projects relative to maintenance prioritization. Prevents C from outpacing L_f_active recovery.
L5.effect_on_model: reduces dC/dt, holds beta_eff stable, slows Em growth — buys time for L_f_active recovery
L5.note: Not permanent. Once Phi drops below 0.7 and L_f_active trajectory is positive, expansion can resume at controlled rate.

L6.authority_note: Decentralization touches system architecture and usually interconnection agreements.
L6.reversibility_note: Coupling exhibits ratchet behavior — it is far easier to add than to remove. Decoupling decisions are close to permanent.
L6.name: kappa_reduction
L6.description: Reduce system coupling through decentralization. Decreases cascade probability and lowers effective beta_eff.
L6.note: Kappa has ratchet character. Positive restoring force requires deliberate structural redesign, not just operational change.
L6.effect_on_model: reduces kappa in F=kappa*Phi and in beta_eff=beta0+gamma*kappa — doubly beneficial

L7.authority_note: Compensation structure requires a board or a regulator. This is the highest-consent lever in the set and the slowest to bite.
L7.name: management_incentive_realignment
L7.description: Couple executive compensation to physical infrastructure reliability metrics rather than purely financial yield proxies.
L7.note: Management ideology shift time constant is 5-15 years. Constraint change is faster than belief change. Focus on structural incentive levers, not persuasion.
L7.effect_on_model: reduces Y_bias, increases S_weight in dC/dt — slows complexity growth and increases maintenance prioritization over time

transition_layer.description: The seven levers act on the physical-labor system. They assume an actor already permitted to pull them. This section models the governing and financial substrate that grants or withholds that permission, and the active steps that carry it from the incumbent design to the target design. Added 2026-08-15; see ledger F-009 for why the framework was incomplete without it.
transition_layer.why_this_layer_exists: Ranking levers by impact and time constant implies the binding constraint is knowing which lever to pull. It is not. L1 and L4 — the two highest-leverage levers in the set — need no external consent at all, while L3 and L7 need a legislature or a board. A framework that does not carry the consent dimension will route a reader with no institutional authority toward levers they cannot pull, and away from the ones they can. That is a design defect, not a missing nicety.

authority_tiers.0: No external consent. A crew, a community, a union local, or a single competent person acting inside their own scope. Cannot be withheld because it was never granted.
authority_tiers.1: Site or crew-lead scope. Work assignment, sequencing, local practice.
authority_tiers.2: Firm, board, or municipal scope. Capital allocation, architecture, interconnection.
authority_tiers.3: State or federal scope. Statute, accreditation, licensure, compensation regulation.

governance.incumbent: permission_before_response — local action requires central authorization in advance. Response latency is the authorization latency, which is uncoupled from the constraint timescale.
governance.target: response_then_audit — local nodes respond within a declared scope and log it; central authority audits afterward and retains the power to rule the response invalid.
governance.note: The target is not the absence of central authority. It is central authority that validates after the fact instead of blocking before it. An authority that cannot resource its audit within its declared window has exited the scope of its claim — that is what audit_authority_scope.py computes.

regulatory.incumbent: rule_applied_outside_declared_scope — regulations written for an operating envelope continue to be enforced after conditions have left that envelope, producing the harm the rule was written to prevent.
regulatory.target: scope_conditional_enforcement — every rule carries its operating envelope; when conditions exit it, the rule is suspended for that situation while its first-principle intent is preserved.

corporate.incumbent: charter_as_permanent_grant — operating privilege treated as unconditional and indefinite.
corporate.target: charter_as_conditional_permission — operating privilege conditioned on serving community function, with a declared crisis response threshold and a contingency that activates on failure to meet it.

financial.incumbent: tier_3_proxy_metrics_govern — capital allocation and executive incentive are driven by financial signals, which measurement.json classifies as the slowest and most filtered tier. Marginal-regime degradation is structurally invisible to them.
financial.target: tier_1_physical_metrics_route_directly_to_the_decision_layer, in parallel with financial reporting and explicitly compared against it.
financial.sequencing_note: Coupling compensation to a physical metric before the metric is trusted and instrumented produces measurement gaming, not measurement. The dashboard must exist and be believed before L7 is pulled. This mirrors the B_i-before-activation constraint at the financial layer: build the credible channel first, then attach consequences to it.

labor.incumbent: credential_as_gate — the ability to practice is granted by credential possession, independent of demonstrated capacity.
labor.note: The last step is deliberately last. A tier-3 ask backed by a tier-0 evidence record is a different ask than a tier-3 ask backed by an argument.

transition_layer.general_pattern: Every substrate transition in this table has the same shape: build the parallel channel at tier 0, run it until it produces a record, and only then make the tier-2 or tier-3 ask using that record as the argument. This is the same structure as the B_i-before-activation constraint (ledger F-004) applied to institutions rather than to nodes — establish the credible channel before attaching consequence to it, or the attempt confirms the prior it was meant to overturn.
transition_layer.evidence_note: Every effort, effect, and authority-tier value in this section is asserted from the structure of the levers, not measured. No transition in this table has been observed running. The numbers are a harness for disagreement, not a result — override them and rerun. See ledger F-010.

lever_interaction_matrix.description: Key coupling relationships between levers. Interventions are not independent.

interactions.description: L4 must precede L1. Reverse order causes re-suppression.
Older node deployment creates field-credible validators for L3 competency assessment.
Older nodes as trusted referrers accelerate L1 lateral network traversal.
Complexity throttle buys time for L1 activation to take effect before Phi crosses threshold.
Regional decentralization increases value of locally-deployed high-R_i hub nodes.
Competency validation (L3) works only if results are visible and credited (L4).

stable_capacity_building_mode.monitoring: track dPhi/dt — if positive and accelerating, escalate to marginal mode before threshold

marginal_stabilization_mode.critical_check: Is B_i assessed and reduction underway before L1 outreach? If not, halt L1 until confirmed.

emergency_mode.note: Single-lever approaches will fail. Coupled deployment required. Accept that some levers will be imperfect — imperfect simultaneous action outperforms perfect sequential action at Phi > 1.0.

monitoring_protocol.false_negative_risk: Financial metrics will not show marginal regime until late. Physical field metrics and labor flow metrics required. tau_management_lag is high-pass filter on decay signal.
